stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, standard in modern LLM deployment.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: SpaceX intends to invest up to $100 billion in massive Louisiana spaceport
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: SpaceX plans a massive investment of up to $100 billion in a new spaceport in Louisiana.
The project is described as being of unprecedented scale.
This signals a major expansion and commitment by SpaceX to large-scale space infrastructure development.

stories.title: New bootloader lets you take the "Meta" out of the original Meta Quest
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: A new bootloader exploit has been discovered for the original Meta Quest.
The vulnerability allows for privilege escalation, granting users 'full control' over the device.
This exploit enables users to bypass Meta's servers and proprietary applications.

stories.title: LAION-BVD: A 10-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training
stories.author: Matthias Bethge
bullet_points: Introduction of LAION-BVD, a massive, open-source video dataset for multimodal AI training.
The dataset comprises 80 million videos totaling 10 million hours, sourced from CommonCrawl.
It is specifically designed for multimodal pre-training across video, audio, and image modalities, with synthetic caption generation.

stories.title: LAION-BVD: A 10-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training
stories.author: Matthias Bethge
bullet_points: Introduction of LAION-BVD, a massive open video dataset designed for multimodal learning.
The dataset comprises 80 million videos totaling 10 million hours, sourced from CommonCrawl.
It supports multimodal pre-training across video, audio, and image modalities, with synthetic caption generation used for training.

stories.title: OpenAI Jalapeño: Better than Nvidia Blackwell
stories.author: bmulholland
bullet_points: OpenAI is reportedly developing custom silicon, codenamed 'Jalapeño', designed to compete directly with high-end Nvidia hardware like Blackwell.
The news suggests OpenAI claims its proprietary chips can outperform Nvidia processors in specific benchmarks.
This development signals a major industry trend toward large AI labs designing their own specialized hardware to reduce reliance on external suppliers.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a language model.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, suggesting a modern, high-performance architecture.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the mainstream LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model designed specifically for autonomous agents.
The model excels at multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round involved prominent investors including Benchmark, Y Combinator, and 8VC.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving a large community of 8.9 million developers.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and multi-token prediction (MTP).
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
Users benefit from faster response times and reduced memory consumption.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads for Apple hardware.
This is currently available in preview, signaling a significant step toward optimized local AI on macOS.

stories.title: Lab supply companies have been selling antibodies using manipulated images
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Lab supply companies are reportedly selling antibodies that utilize manipulated images.
The extent of the image manipulation is described as widespread among suppliers.
The quality of the fraudulent data is severe enough that it would warrant paper retraction in scientific publications.

stories.title: AI won’t replace radiologists, but it will dramatically change their jobs
stories.author: Lola Butcher, Knowable Magazine
bullet_points: AI is poised to significantly transform the role of radiologists rather than completely replace them.
The article addresses a historical prediction that AI would fully automate radiological roles.
The shift indicates AI will become a powerful augmentation tool in medical diagnostics.

stories.title: Apple's new desktop computers are designed specifically for local AI development
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Apple's new desktop computers are specifically engineered to support local AI development.
The hardware refresh addresses the community trend of users daisy-chaining Macs for AI workloads.
This signals a strategic shift by Apple to integrate and optimize hardware for on-device machine learning.

stories.title: Reading Is Not Using: Retrieval, Judgment, and the Design of AI Financial Research Workflows
stories.author: Zhizhe Liu
bullet_points: Identifies a critical 'retrieval-integration gap' in how LLMs are used for financial analysis.
Current evaluation methods focus too much on information retrieval rather than the actual impact of retrieved data on AI judgment.
Research explores how varying context length (up to 128k tokens) affects the influence of specific risk disclosures in financial LLM workflows.

stories.title: What FID Hides: Detecting, Ranking, and Diagnosing Deviations in Generative Evaluation
stories.author: Hao Chen
bullet_points: The paper critiques the limitations of standard generative model evaluation metrics like FID and KID.
It highlights that FID's reliance on only the first two moments can obscure significant distributional differences in generated samples.
The research proposes methods for detecting, ranking, and diagnosing deviations in generative model performance beyond simple scalar scores.

stories.title: Effective Learning Rate Governs Loss Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
stories.author: Lei Wu
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of Effective Learning Rate (ELR) as the primary governor of loss dynamics in language model pretraining.
Demonstrates that matching ELR across different runs causes loss trajectories to collapse, even when raw learning rates and parameter norms differ significantly.
Indicates that this ELR dependency holds robustly across various optimizers, architectures, datasets, and model scales, suggesting a fundamental principle in LLM training.

stories.title: Apple introduces M6 and M5 Ultra
stories.author: interpol_p
bullet_points: Apple has announced the introduction of new high-performance chips, specifically the M6 and M5 Ultra.
The M5 Ultra is highlighted as Apple's most powerful chip to date, indicating a significant leap in processing capability.
The news covers updates across Apple's product line, including comparisons and features for the M6 Mac Mini.

stories.title: FDA authorizes first wearable device that monitors ketone and blood sugar levels
stories.author: sunnynagra
bullet_points: FDA has approved a novel wearable device.
The device is capable of monitoring both ketone and blood sugar levels.
This represents a significant step forward in continuous, non-invasive health monitoring technology.

stories.title: When anyone can build with a prompt, what counts as productivity? — We're moving our whole company to AI and keeping humans on judgment
stories.author: uehara
bullet_points: The rise of prompt-based coding democratizes software creation, making programming accessible to non-experts.
The article discusses a company's strategic shift to integrating AI across its operations.
The core theme explores the evolving definition of 'productivity' in an AI-augmented workforce, emphasizing human judgment.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary AI services and local, open-source LLMs.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Trump is upping the price of Big Tech’s favorite visa
stories.author: Gaby Del Valle
bullet_points: DHS announced a significant fee increase (over $103,000) for H-1B visas.
The State Department plans to revoke visas for up to 200,000 asylum seekers.
The news directly impacts the immigration and labor landscape for Big Tech.

stories.title: The world's busiest spaceport is about to get a lot quieter, at least for now
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX is targeting Starship launches from Florida.
The immediate launch goal is set for the end of the current year.
A more realistic timeline for Starship deployment is projected to be 2027.

stories.title: SPO++: Stream-Aligned Policy Optimization for Asynchronous Agentic RL
stories.author: Zihe Huang
bullet_points: Introduces SPO++: Stream-Aligned Policy Optimization to address inefficiencies in group-relative reinforcement learning for long, variable tool-use trajectories.
Addresses a limitation in Single-stream Policy Optimization (SPO) where trajectory centering fails to properly center the token-weighted actor loss.
The proposed fix involves standardizing the optimization process to correct the mismatch between trajectory centering and token-weighted consumption.

stories.title: FedV-KGQA: Multi-Hop Question Answering over Vertically Partitioned Knowledge Graphs
stories.author: Oshani Seneviratne
bullet_points: Addresses the real-world challenge of distributed knowledge graphs due to data governance and sovereignty.
Introduces FedV-KGQA, a framework designed for multi-hop question answering across vertically partitioned knowledge graphs.
The approach allows organizations to share entities while maintaining ownership over their disjoint sets of relations.

stories.title: Constrained Entity Selection under Partial Knowledge for LLM-Based Knowledge Graph QA
stories.author: Emanuel Kitzelmann
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of LLM-based Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) failing to accurately ground answers.
Proposes a new method focusing on 'Constrained Entity Selection under Partial Knowledge' to improve robustness.
Compares existing methods, noting the brittleness of full semantic parsing (e.g., SPARQL) versus the lack of formal guarantees in pure LLM reasoning.

stories.title: Strictly Causal Streaming Video Anomaly Detection with a Theoretically-Grounded State-Space Core
stories.author: Yogesh Kumar
bullet_points: Introduces a strictly causal streaming video anomaly detector utilizing state-space models (SSMs).
Addresses limitations of prior work by achieving O(1) time and memory complexity per incoming frame.
Focuses on theoretical grounding and edge hardware efficiency, moving beyond simple GPU throughput benchmarks.

stories.title: Automatic Model Card Generation Using an LLM
stories.author: Cor-Paul Bezemer
bullet_points: The paper addresses the lack of standardized and consistent documentation (Model Cards) for machine learning models.
It introduces MCTidy, an LLM-based approach designed to reorganize existing, unstructured model cards into a standardized template.
The goal is to enhance transparency, usability, and comparability across different ML models.

stories.title: StarHarness: Evolving Harnesses with Stratified Search for Enterprise Environments
stories.author: Sagar Davasam
bullet_points: StarHarness is a new framework designed to evolve agent harnesses for specific enterprise environments.
It allows for customization of agent components (prompts, tools, skills, subagent structure) without altering the core model weights.
The framework employs stratified search and task separation to efficiently manage the evolution and evaluation process.

stories.title: BioKERN: Biological Kernel Regularization for Histology-to-Transcriptomics Neighborhood Retrieval
stories.author: Betul Orcan-Ekmekci
bullet_points: BioKERN is a new multimodal spatial representation-learning framework designed for histology-to-transcriptomics data.
It addresses a limitation in existing methods by explicitly incorporating biological neighborhood structure as a learnable inductive bias.
The goal is to preserve spatial context between non-paired spots, moving beyond simple instance-level matching.

stories.title: A Geometric Theory of Robust Fairness Audits
stories.author: Binita Maity
bullet_points: The paper addresses the lack of robustness in neighborhood-based fairness audits used in ML.
These audits are sensitive to small feature space perturbations, which can change local neighborhoods and fairness assessments.
The authors propose a new geometric framework to analyze the robustness of these fairness auditing procedures.

stories.title: LION: A Clifford Neural Paradigm for Multimodal-Attributed Graph Learning
stories.author: Guoren Wang
bullet_points: The research introduces LION, a new Clifford Neural Paradigm designed for Multimodal-Attributed Graph Learning.
The shift to multimodal-attributed graphs is noted as a significant trend enhancing data representation in Graph ML.
Current neural paradigms are limited, particularly in neglecting context during modality alignment, which LION aims to address.

stories.title: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces 'BrowserForge,' a method to scale web agent training by using parallel browser sandboxes.
Addresses the data scarcity problem for training web agents that rely on visual (pixel-based) interaction rather than HTML parsing.
Aims to overcome the limitations of current datasets, which are small and drawn from narrow sets of websites.

stories.title: Reading Is Not Using: Retrieval, Judgment, and the Design of AI Financial Research Workflows
stories.author: Zhizhe Liu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical gap in evaluating LLMs used for financial analysis: current metrics focus on retrieval accuracy rather than the impact of retrieved information on final judgments.
It investigates the 'retrieval-integration gap' in long-context financial analysis, where the quality of context integration is not adequately tested.
Experimental findings show that the influence of risk disclosures on AI judgments changes significantly when varying the amount of unrelated context provided to the LLM.

stories.title: Linear Probing Provides Robust and Efficient Detection of Machine-Generated Text
stories.author: Elena Simperl
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need to distinguish machine-generated text (MGT) from human-written text (HWT) due to misuse concerns.
The study proposes that simple linear probes are highly effective and sample-efficient for MGT detection, outperforming complex supervised detectors.
A key finding is that the latent representations of MGT and HWT exhibit linearity, which underpins the effectiveness of the linear probing method.

stories.title: ExpConCAD: Experience-Guided Text-to-CAD Generation from Shape Descriptions with Implicit Spatial Constraints
stories.author: See-Kiong Ng
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of underspecified natural-language descriptions in Text-to-CAD generation.
Proposes a method (ExpConCAD) to infer missing spatial constraints based on construction structure and design experience.
Focuses on moving Text-to-CAD from simple generation to producing valid, executable CAD programs.

stories.title: The RAT: A Unified Bayesian Model for RAG Evaluation
stories.author: Jan Deriu
bullet_points: Introduces 'The RAT,' a new unified Bayesian model specifically designed for evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.
The framework jointly models key pipeline components: retrieval success, answer correctness, and abstention behavior.
It offers a detailed analysis by factorizing the model according to the information flow within the RAG pipeline, distinguishing various types of task success.

stories.title: Method, Mind, and Morality: How People Make Sense of Artificial Intelligence
stories.author: James Evans
bullet_points: The research investigates how humans are making sense of the rapid advancement and impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI).
It utilizes a mixed-methods approach, combining computational text analysis of millions of articles/posts with 57 semi-structured interviews.
The study specifically tracks shifts in public and professional understanding before and after the recent surge in AI interest, identifying sociological frames.

stories.title: SkillForge: Evolving Verifiable Skills for Reinforcement Learning Agents
stories.author: Xiangxiang Chu
bullet_points: SkillForge addresses a limitation in RL agents by introducing verifiable skills for complex decision-making.
It improves upon existing skill-based RL methods (like SkillRL) by verifying the effectiveness of stored skills.
The research focuses on enabling RL agents to accumulate reusable knowledge across multiple episodes, moving beyond episodic training.

stories.title: The M5 Ultra Mac Studio: I Did the Math So You Don't Have To
stories.author: arshtechpro
bullet_points: Apple has announced the new Mac Studio lineup.
The new models feature the M5 Max and the first M5 Ultra chip.
The article provides a technical analysis ('did the math') of the new hardware.

stories.title: Weir - deterministic unit tests for AI agents (no LLM)
stories.author: idogol24
bullet_points: Introduces 'Weir,' a tool for creating deterministic unit tests specifically for AI agents.
Addresses a critical security/reliability gap where agent logs might falsely report success despite internal failures or hijacking.
Highlights the focus on testing agent logic without relying on large language models (LLMs) for validation.
